svg.title: Rung 9's learning test on the current model: MBON11's responses before and after pairing each odor with dopamine
svg.text: Rung 9's learning test on the current model, recorded
Pairing 3-octanol with dopamine cuts MBON11's response to it 89% (flies 80%) and to 4-methylcyclohexanol 38% (flies 27%), as rung 9 asks.
Pairing 4-methylcyclohexanol cuts its own 98% (flies 76%) but 3-octanol's only 10% (flies 38%): its 87 Kenyon cells hold 8% of 3-octanol's 562 (flies 30%).
And the responses are brief. To 3-octanol MBON11 peaks as high as flies' (144 spikes/s; flies 135-140), but 79% of its evoked spikes come in the first 0.3 s;
from 0.5 s to the odor's end it fires 12 spikes/s where flies' holds 95-100. So it gains a third of flies' spikes (39 against 118), and to 4-methylcyclohexanol 8.5 (flies 110).

svg.text: flies before pairing (Hige et al. 2015, read off Fig. 1E)
The model: mean of 4 seeds of 8 flies, smoothed as Hige et al. smoothed theirs (a Gaussian, SD 50 ms, which also spreads each rise earlier). Evoked spikes: 0-1.4 s, above the rest.
